q-124179.name: Question 1
q-124179.worked_solution:
Let $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation. 

For line integrals with respect to $y,$ we have the following properties:

- ${\int }_{-C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y=-{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

- ${\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-3+5 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

q-124179.html:
Question 1
?

If ∫−C1f(x,y)dy=3 and ∫C2f(x,y)dy=5, calculate ∫Cf(x,y)dy given that C=C1∪C2.

a
−2
b
7
c
2
d
Impossible to determine
e
8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let C=C1∪C2 be a piecewise smooth path in the xy-plane, and let −C be the curve consisting of the same points as C but with the opposite orientation.

For line integrals with respect to y, we have the following properties:

  • ∫−Cf(x,y)dy=−∫Cf(x,y)dy

  • ∫Cf(x,y)dy=∫C1f(x,y)dy+∫C2f(x,y)dy

In our case, we have

∫Cf(x,y)dy=∫C1f(x,y)dy+∫C2f(x,y)dy=−∫−C1f(x,y)dy+∫C2f(x,y)dy=−3+5=2.

q-124281.name: Question 2
q-124281.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130455/assets/6b095a29b433107c37cd7e28c853d9d3d3547fb64a9e874783206b86c0aca6c1.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x,$ where $C$ is the path along a quarter circle of radius $3,$ traversed from the point $(1,-3)$ to the point $(4,0),$ shown above.
q-124281.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $x$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $x$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1},
$$

where ${x}_{2}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${x}_{1}$ is the $x$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${x}_{2}=4$ and ${x}_{1}=1.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}x={x}_{2}-{x}_{1}=4-1=3.
$$

q-124336.html:
Question 5
?

Calculate ∫Cdy, where C=C1∪C2 is the path comprising of two line segments, as shown above.

a
5+52
b
−5
c
5
d
−1
e
1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The line integral of unity with respect to y along a path C is equal to the net change in y between the terminal and initial points:

∫Cdy=y2−y1, where y2 is the y-coordinate of the terminal point, and y1 is the y-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, y2=0 and y1=−1. Therefore,

∫Cdy=y2−y1=0−(−1)=1.
